title: Safety-net controller for multi-region failover with probabilistic readiness probes
creator: Ava Morales
description: Design and implement a lightweight safety-net controller that coordinates multi-region failover. The controller will run probabilistic readiness probes and selective cold-start warmups against standby pools to minimize recovery latency while avoiding unnecessary cost and capacity churn. This ticket covers probe scheduling heuristics, circuit-breaker integration, rollout knobs for tiered customers, and observability hooks for SLO correlation.
acceptance_criteria: Controller deploys as a non-blocking service in control plane and can be toggled per-customer via feature flag
Readiness probes run with configurable probability and adaptive backoff; probe results feed into a health score (0-100) per standby pool
Controller exposes a REST endpoint returning pool health scores and last-probe timestamps
Failover orchestration consumes health scores to prevent false activation: require score >= 80 for promotion unless manual override
Integration tests simulate region outages and show median failover latency improvement of >= 25% for high-priority customers compared to baseline
Dashboard panels added to Console (per-customer and per-region) showing probe coverage, probe cost, and promotion decisions
steps: Design probe types: lightweight TCP/HTTP handshake, short tokenized model warmup, and KV-cache verification
Prototype probabilistic scheduler (Poisson sampling) that targets N probes/day with jitter per pool
Define health scoring algorithm and thresholds for automatic promotion vs. manual escalation
Implement controller REST API and feature-flag gating per customer and tier
Add metrics and traces: probe_latency_ms, probe_success, health_score, promotion_decisions, probe_cost_tokens
Create integration test harness that injects synthetic latency and capacity drain into a standby region
Run canary on internal account set, iterate on probe frequency to balance cost and readiness
decisions: Use probabilistic probes (configurable sample rate) rather than deterministic full-fashion checks to control cost at scale
Health score to combine probe success rate, recent successful warmups, and available capacity with configurable weights
Default promotion threshold set to 80 to reduce noisy activations; allow per-customer overrides for enterprise SLAs
Controller keeps a short-lived in-memory cache of recent probe results to avoid duplicate probes during cascade events
Circuit-breaker ties into runtime autoscaler to prevent triggering promotions when target pool has insufficient headroom
